title: Build half a product, not a half-assed product
coreMove: Shrink the promise until your team can honor it fully; partial excellence on a narrow scope beats broad mediocrity, so cut the merely good to make one thing great.

exampleSpecs.audience: makers tempted to match a competitor's feature count
exampleSpecs.stakes: match the enterprise feature bulk or honor a narrow promise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist chooses narrow completeness over matching a rival's feature list

exampleSpecs.audience: teams that protect every defensible idea
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep three good features or cut two to perfect one
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sacrifices a merely-good idea to make one piece great

exampleSpecs.audience: operators who plan as if effort were unlimited
exampleSpecs.stakes: keep a sprawling menu or sacrifice scope to a few dishes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist accepts that limited capacity requires real sacrifice

exampleSpecs.audience: teams that mistake sloppiness for focus
exampleSpecs.stakes: ship a rough narrowed product or finish the chosen half well
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist fixes the misreading that focus excuses incompleteness

exampleSpecs.stakes: spread polish evenly or concentrate craft where it is felt
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist directs craft to the parts customers actually experience

exampleSpecs.audience: product leads chasing parity with rivals
exampleSpecs.stakes: add a feature to match a rival or hold a whole promise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist measures completeness against the promise, not the rival

exampleSpecs.audience: teams that gauge strength by feature count
exampleSpecs.stakes: grow the feature count or make the core promise feel whole
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist replaces feature count with a wholeness test
